{{Short description|Extinct bird genus}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range =
[[Middle Miocene]], ~{{fossilrange|15|11.6}} | image = | image_caption = | display_parents = 2 | genus = Shargaotis | parent_authority = Zelenkov, [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = ignipes | authority = Zelenkov, 2026 }} '''''Shargaotis''''' ({{lit|[[Sharga, Govi-Altai|Sharga]] ''[[Otis (bird)|Otis]]''}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of bird in the family [[Otididae]] (bustards), known the [[Middle Miocene]] of Mongolia. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Shargaotis ignipes''''', known from a fragment of a [[tibiotarsus]]. ''Shargaotis'' is most similar to the [[Neontology|extant]] genera ''[[Otis (bird)|Otis]]'' and ''[[Chlamydotis]]'', and is among the oldest known bustards in the fossil record. == Discovery and naming == The ''Shargaotis'' fossil material was discovered at the '[[Sharga, Govi-Altai|Sharga]] locality', representing Miocene-dated outcrops in western Mongolia. It was collected as part of the Soviet / Russian–Mongolian Paleontological Expeditions, which were conducted in 1978, 1979, 1984, and 2001. The specimen is housed at the [[Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences|Paleontological Institute]], part of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen PIN, no. 4869/249. The specimen consists of the [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|distal]]most (toward the bottom) end of the left [[tibiotarsus]], a lower leg bone. In 2026, Russian palaeornithologist Nikita V. Zelenkov [[Species description|described]] ''Shargaotis ignipes'' as a new genus and species of extinct bustard based on these fossil remains, establishing PIN, no. 4869/249 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Shargaotis'', combines a reference to the [[Type locality (biology)|type locality]] (Sharga) with ''Otis'', the generic name of the closely related extant [[great bustard]] (''Otis tarda''). The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''ignipes'', is derived from [[Latin]] roots meaning {{gloss|fiery-footed}}, and by extension, {{gloss|extremely fast}}. This alludes to the [[Slavs|Slavic]] name for bustards, which is derived from a [[Proto-Slavic]] word meaning {{gloss|fast-running bird}}. Three additional isolated bustard bone fragments are known from the Sharga locality, including PIN, no. 4869/250, a distal left tibiotarsus distinct from that of ''Shargaotis''. This specimen is most similar to the extant bustard ''[[Lophotis]]''. The second specimen, PIN, no. 4659/248, is the distal end of a [[carpometacarpus]], likely belonging to an individual larger than the ''S. ignipes'' holotype. The third specimen, PIN, no. 4869/235, is the base [[Phalanx bone|phalanx]] forming the major wing finger. All three of these specimens were referred to Otididae gen. indet. (genus indeterminate) as they can not be referred to ''Shargaotis'' due to a lack of overlapping material with the holotype. However, the similarity of the latter two to ''Chlamydotis'' suggests they may be referrable to this taxon. Regardless, the existence of multiple bustard taxa in a single ecosystem would not be surprising, as this is observed in modern faunas. == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Zelenkov |first1=N.
